action: Run the emergency council session with a structured agenda that forces actual votes, not just discussion. Agenda: (1) Authorize a $150,000 Emergency Workforce Transition Fund drawn from the municipal reserve fund — disbursed as direct retraining grants up to $2,500 per affected worker, partnered with Millfield Community College for EV certification, CDL upgrading, and basic tech skills tracks; criteria: documented employment in transportation, auto sales, repair, or adjacent services within the past 12 months. (2) Authorize a $75,000 Small Business Stabilization Grant program — grants up to $5,000 per business, capped at businesses with under 15 employees and documented revenue decline of 15% or more since baseline spending index; application window opens immediately, reviewed by a three-person committee. (3) Vote to require RoboRide to obtain a municipal operating license before Phase 2 launch — license conditions include a local impact fee of $0.25 per ride directed into the workforce fund, quarterly employment impact reporting, and a local hiring preference clause for any human support roles. (4) Formally establish the Economic Transition Task Force with a 90-day charter, monthly public reporting, and seats for one auto worker representative, one small business owner, one community organizer, and two council members. Bring all four items to a roll-call vote before adjournment.
